subject: Unbilled sessions and transaction trace request — July invoice
messages:
From: Lydia Chang <lydia@opsdata.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: OpsData Billing <billing@opsdata.ai>
Date: 2027-07-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: July invoice question — unbilled sessions

Hi Mina,

We received our July invoice and noticed a discrepancy between our telemetry and the billed session lines. The attached CSV is our internal snapshot (UTC timestamps) for July 14–15; you can see ~1,120 sessions attributed to our production API key but only 985 sessions billed on the invoice PDF you sent. The delta is ~135 sessions (~12%).

We rely on accurate session attribution for our revenue mapping; can you confirm whether there was an ingestion window or bucketing change on Redwood's side last week? If possible, please provide a per-request export for the disputed window and any guidance on how billing buckets are determined (cutoff times, timezone handling, streaming sessions that span windows).

Attachments: opsdata-usage-snapshot-20270714.csv

Thanks,
Lydia
Billing Operations
OpsData Analytics

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chang <lydia@opsdata.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: July invoice question — unbilled sessions

Thanks Lydia — I pulled this into our queue. Quick initial notes: we did a minor metering rollout on 2027-07-14 related to streaming-session termination semantics (internal change to when we flush KV caches and finalize session buckets). That rollout was targeted and reportedly non-breaking, but it could affect sessions that closed right at midnight UTC.

Could you send 3–5 sample request_ids and the approximate timestamps for sessions you think are missing? That will let us pull raw traces and check the metering timeline. I'll loop in Ben to run the trace extraction and Markus for the billing decision.

If it's our rollout that caused an undercount, we'll determine a remediation (export of raw logs + pro-rated credit or invoice adjustment).

—Mina
Product Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Lydia Chang <lydia@opsdata.ai>
Date: 2027-07-16T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: July invoice question — unbilled sessions

On Fri, Jul 15, 2027 at 10:05 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Lydia — I pulled this into our queue. Quick initial notes: we did a minor metering rollout on 2027-07-14 related to streaming-session termination semantics ...

Hi all — I pulled the request_id samples Lydia provided in a follow-up (see quoted below) and ran them through the backend trace extractor. Preliminary findings:

- Several of the sessions in OpsData's snapshot have finalization timestamps between 2027-07-14T23:58:00Z and 2027-07-15T00:02:30Z. Our billing window for daily aggregation is 00:00:00–23:59:59 UTC, but the rollout changed the finalization event to fire after the session close when KV caches flush asynchronously.
- That caused a small set of sessions (>120 in the export) to be assigned to the next calendar day in our billing table, which could appear as "unbilled" if OpsData compared a slice that stopped at 2027-07-14T23:59:59 UTC while the actual billing attributed them to 2027-07-15.

Actionable next steps I recommend:
1) We'll produce a raw per-request export for the disputed window (CSV) including request_id, start_ts, end_ts, billing_bucket_date, and billed_tokens.
2) If the attribution mismatch is confirmed, propose an invoice correction line for the affected sessions or a one-time credit.

I've attached a short session trace for one sample (session-trace-20270714.txt) to illustrate the delayed finalization event.

—Ben
Billing Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachment: session-trace-20270714.txt

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lydia Chang <lydia@opsdata.ai>
Date: 2027-07-18T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: July invoice question — unbilled sessions

Thanks team. I reviewed Ben's traces. Short summary for Lydia and OpsData:

- Root cause: rollout changed the timing of the session-finalize event, which in edge cases shifts the billing_bucket_date by one day for sessions that closed within ~3 minutes of UTC midnight.
- Scope: based on a quick scan, ~130–145 sessions for OpsData across the 14–15 July boundary were affected.

Customer-facing remediation options:
A) Retroactively reassign affected sessions to the original bucket and issue an invoice adjustment (line-item credit).
B) Leave billing unchanged but issue a one-time credit equivalent to the charges for the affected sessions.

Recommendation: offer option B as the faster path to resolution while we finish a safe backfill for A. For OpsData's size this is about a $1,140 credit if we use standard per-session pricing — I suggest we offer a 100% credit to expedite collection closure. If OpsData prefers A, we'll need ~3 business days to run the backfill and update ledger entries.

If OpsData agrees, I'll prepare the credit and an evidence bundle (export + traces) and we can apply it to the July invoice. Happy to hop on a 20-minute screen-share to walk through the evidence.

—Markus
VP Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Lydia Chang <lydia@opsdata.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-20T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: July invoice question — unbilled sessions

Thanks — this all makes sense and we appreciate the quick investigation. OpsData is fine with a one-time credit (option B) to reconcile July while you complete the backfill. Can you: 

1) Share the per-request export CSV for our records (we logged it as evidence for internal auditors).
2) Confirm the credit amount and when it will reflect on our account (we have month-end close next Friday).
3) Provide a short note we can attach to our bookkeeping stating root cause = metering-window attribution change during a rollout on 2027-07-14.

We'll take the screen-share if you think it's helpful, but the export + confirmation of credit timing will be enough.

Attachments: redwood-invoice-July2027.pdf (for reference)

Best,
Lydia
